attribution_text: NASA Asteroids NeoWs, provided through NASA's Open APIs and NASA/JPL asteroid-team data as documented by NASA. Lumina presents the source-provided near-Earth close-approach estimates without adding impact-risk calculations.
authentication_method: A registered NASA API key is required for production synchronization and is supplied only as the server-side LUMINA_NASA_API_KEY secret. DEMO_KEY is not accepted.
cache_ttl: Fresh for 3 hours after a successful retrieval; stale-if-error for the following 12 hours; expired thereafter. A successful retrieval schedules the next refresh after 2 hours.
contact_or_user_agent_requirement: Lumina sends a fixed identifying User-Agent without personal data. A SecretStr API key is carried only by the typed in-memory sync request, inserted at the final transport boundary, and never serialized into diagnostics, jobs, metrics, status, cache, quarantine, or public output.
failure_and_fallback_behaviour: Reject malformed, oversized, out-of-window, duplicate, non-Earth, or contract-breaking responses, quarantine bounded evidence, retain the last-known-good cache, and expose stale data explicitly only during the approved stale-if-error interval. Never substitute unrelated data.
fetch_time_policy: Each accepted seven-date cache entry records the UTC retrieval time and freshness deadlines; no live snapshot DataManifest is generated.
fixture_and_checksum_strategy: Offline tests use sanitized deterministic NeoWs feed fixtures with multiple date buckets, ordinary and potentially hazardous classifications, optional additive provider fields, and hostile-input cases. Accepted responses are hashed over their exact bounded raw bytes with SHA-256; complete quarantined evidence is bounded and redacts any API-key value before storage and hashing.
known_limitations: The v1 provider is NeoWs feed-only and does not perform lookup, browse, JPL CAD, SBDB, or Sentry requests.
NeoWs does not provide a source-backed close-approach distance or time uncertainty interval in the approved feed contract used by Lumina v1; Lumina does not synthesize one.
NeoWs close-approach time is preserved as provider text without relabeling it as UTC, TDB, TT, or local time because the reviewed feed contract does not establish that time scale.
Diameter values are the NeoWs estimated meter range and are not presented as measured diameter or an uncertainty interval.
PHA is preserved from the NeoWs boolean and is not recomputed; it is a technical classification and not an impact prediction.
The product is a bounded current seven-date feed projection with a maximum public projection of 32 encounters, not a historical catalogue or impact-risk product.
observation_or_publication_time_policy: The approach date and close-approach time text are NeoWs provider values for the selected event. Lumina preserves the text and does not silently convert or attach a time-scale label; the UTC retrieval timestamp and cache freshness state are separate facts.
purpose: Low-volume production synchronization of NASA Asteroids NeoWs Earth close-approach events for Lumina's Near-Earth Objects surface.
rate_or_fair_use_constraints: One global provider lease, at most one successful refresh every two hours, hourly recovery enqueue opportunities, at most three closed-circuit attempts with deterministic 1-second and 2-second spacing, bounded request cycles, a fixed seven-date request window, and no browser-direct NASA traffic.
refresh_schedule: External deployment cron enqueues provider.sync once per UTC hour; the provider performs network I/O only when its two-hour refresh eligibility is due.
